props.title: Big Buck Bunny
props.initialSlug: Gentle giant bunny fights back against bullying critters

sections.content: Big Buck Bunny (2008) revolutionized open-source animation by proving free software could create professional-quality 3D films. Created using Blender, this charming short about a gentle giant rabbit facing off against bullying rodents demonstrated the power of community-driven animation. Its impact echoes through later open projects like Sintel (2010) and Cosmos Laundromat (2015), establishing a new model for collaborative digital filmmaking. The film's technical achievements influenced indie animation studios, showing how sophisticated character rigging and fur simulation could be achieved without proprietary software.

sections.content: The production process of Big Buck Bunny broke new ground for collaborative animation. The Blender Foundation assembled a small team in Amsterdam, documenting every step publicly and releasing all assets and source files - unprecedented transparency that influenced projects like Glass Half (2015) and Agent 327 (2017). This open approach created a valuable teaching tool for aspiring animators worldwide.

The film's character design deserves special attention. Big Buck's deceptively simple appearance masks sophisticated technical work in fur dynamics and facial expressions. This influenced later open-source characters like those in Tears of Steel (2012) and helped establish best practices for character rigging in Blender that are still used today. SUBHEAD: Impact on Independent Animation

Big Buck Bunny sparked a movement in independent animation that continues with projects like Spring (2019) and Coffee Run (2020). Its success proved that small teams could create professional-quality animation without massive studio resources. The film's creative commons license meant animators could legally study, reuse, and learn from its production files - creating an unprecedented educational resource.
